title: Meta introduces Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent - TechCrunch
summary: Meta's Muse agents continue to get new features and integrations. Spaces promises to be a new way to interact with the AI helpers.

Meta introduces Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent Lucas Ropek 10:44 AM PST · November 6, 2026 Meta recently launched its Muse agents — a new generation of cuddly agentic helpers. Now, the company has launched Spaces, a new way to communicate and collaborate with them.

As far as I can tell, Spaces are basically breakout conversations that revolve around a particular topic — although Meta refers to them as “custom experiences.” They live in the sidebar of the interface where you interact with your Muse agent. Clicking on the Space brings up the conversation, where Muse works toward a particular goal on your behalf.

For instance, if you wanted to plan a vacation, you could open a new Space focused on that particular project, and whenever you want to work on it with Muse, you would click to open that particular tab. Or, if you’re focused on collecting recipes for an upcoming family event, you’d open a new Space for that particular project. Other examples Meta gives are a holiday gift tracker, a wedding planner, or a space for DIY projects.

“Describe an idea in chat, and Muse builds a space for you, whether that’s a tracker, a planner or a project board,” Meta says.

Spaces can also be easily integrated with third-party apps and information, Meta says.

title: PSA: Want To Learn Link's Ocarina Tunes? Nintendo's Got The Sheet Music For All Of Them - Nintendo Life
text:
Whether you have been playing Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, watching the trailers, or just been in the ether of its release, you almost certainly have an ocarina melody or two stuck in your head right now. For those who want to channel their earworm into a lesson, Nintendo has shared the sheet music for each of Link's in-game tunes, so you can stop whistling Zelda's Lullaby and learn to play it instead.

Nintendo previously announced that it'd share music how-tos via the Zelda Notes app, so you could work out how to play the tunes on any real-world ocarinas you may have accumulated over the years. But look, all of them are also available on the game's Japanese website , so you don't need to worry about unlocking them in-game before you start learning!

Alongside the sheet music, the website also includes specific ocarina finger placement to follow along with on the titular instrument.

Oh yes, and just in case these 12 tunes aren't already ingrained in your heads, the site (and app) also features a handy 'Play' button, so you can listen to how each of them is meant to sound before taking a stab at 'em yourself.

Of course, you might be waiting to learn any of these until you have one of the official tie-in ocarinas in your hands. Pre-orders for HORI's electric model went live back in September, and we are now seeing orders slowly trickle out for the playable version in select regional Nintendo stores.

title: Apple Rumored to Drop the iPhone's Action Button Next Year - MacRumors
summary: Apple plans to merge the iPhone's Action button with the Camera Control starting next year, according to the leaker known as "Instant Digital". In a new post on Weibo, the leaker claimed that a single press of the combined button would open the camera, while a long press would trigger the function assigned to the Action button. They explicitly clarified that the dedicated Action button would disappear, while the Camera Control button would remain.
text:
Apple plans to merge the iPhone's Action button with the Camera Control starting next year, according to the leaker known as " Instant Digital ."

In a new post on Weibo, the leaker claimed that a single press of the combined button would open the camera, while a long press would trigger the function assigned to the Action button. They explicitly clarified that the dedicated Action button would disappear, while the Camera Control button would remain.

The proposed arrangement seems plausible given how the two features already work. The Action button predates the Camera Control and requires a long press to activate its assigned function, while a single press of the Camera Control opens the camera. Combining them in the way described would therefore preserve both familiar interactions, with the customizable action simply moving to a different location on the device.

A long press of Camera Control currently opens Visual Intelligence , but that feature has since been integrated directly into the Camera app as Siri mode in iOS 27 . That integration could give Apple room to reassign the gesture while keeping Visual Intelligence accessible through the Camera app.

It is notable that the iPhone Duo also lacks an Action button , despite retaining Camera Control. Its omission provides a precedent for an iPhone without the separate control and could hint at a broader change in the future.

title: MacBook Pro M6 Review: A Slight Upgrade, But Still The Most Accessible MacBook Pro - Engadget
summary: The M6 MacBook Pro is more of the same, but that's still pretty great.
text:
Devindra Hardawar for Engadget Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover RATING : 9 / 10 Pros Excellent case Powerful M6 chip Great Liquid Retina display Tons of ports Cons More expensive than before No significant design changes When I reviewed the M5 Max MacBook Pro earlier this year, I predicted that it might soon feel out of date whenever Apple's fabled touchscreen MacBook Pros arrived. That's even more true for the new MacBook Pro with an M6 chip , which was briefly announced last week before the new touchscreen-equipped PROLED XDR MacBook Pros arrived. Those systems are clearly going to get most of the attention this holiday season from Apple's marketing team and deep-pocketed Mac-heads, so where does that leave the lowly entry-level MacBook Pro?

The M6 MacBook Pro is more of the same design we've seen for years, with a slightly faster chip. And yet, at $1,999 , it's still a pretty compelling machine for anyone not crazy enough to spend an extra $900 for an OLED touchscreen and a slightly lighter system. Even Apple's leftovers are still miles ahead of most of the competition.

Devindra Hardawar for Engadget The biggest selling point of this MacBook Pro is Apple's new M6 chip, which we've already seen in the recent Mac mini .
